newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran slams "rebel" Taleban, backs Afghan president.
newsitem.headline: Iran slams "rebel" Taleban, backs Afghan president.

text.p: Iran on Wednesday blasted the radical Islamic Afghan Taleban militia as "rebels", and reiterated its recognition of the government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani, the Iranian news agency IRNA said.

"Iran considers the government of President Burhanuddin Rabbani as the legal representative in Afghanistan and the emergence of a group of rebels, which is being supported by certain countries, does not take away its legitimacy," said Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati, quoted by the agency.
The criticism appeared to be harsher than previous Iranian statements on the Taleban, who seized Kabul last month, driving out forces loyal to Rabbani.

Most Tehran officials had earlier refrained from directly attacking the Taleban which Iranian media have condemned as set up by Pakistan with backing from the United States and funding from Saudi Arabia to counter Iran's influence in the region. Pakistan denies the charges.
Velayati also repeated Iran's stand that Afghan factions should stop fighting and reach a power-sharing accord, IRNA said.
